Public hearing to consider a timely-filed appeal (Case No. APPEAL-008054-2025) of the Planning Commission's determination (Case No. ITRP-007793-2025) that off-premise alcoholic beverage sales for beer and wine cannot be considered an accessory use to a primary retail use within the Limited Local Commercial (L-LC) zone for the property located at 1988 Village Park Way. Environmental Considerations: The action being considered by the City Council is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) because it is not a "project" under Section 15378(b)(5) of CEQA Guidelines. The action involves an organizational or administrative activity of government that will not result in the direct or indirect physical change in the environment. In addition, pursuant to Section 15270 of the CEQA Guidelines, CEQA does not apply to projects which a public agency rejects or disapproves. Contact Person: Associate Planner Carr

Bruce Evans and Affirming the Planning Commission's Determination that the "Alcoholic Beverage, Sales-Off Premises" Land Use Cannot Be Considered as an Accessory Use to the Primary Retail Use in the Limited Local Commercial (L-LC) Zone, for the Property Located at 1988 Village Park Way," affirming the Planning Commission's decision to adopt Resolution No. PC 2025-11 determining that off-premise alcoholic beverage sales of beer and wine cannot be considered an accessory use to a primary retail use within the Limited Local Commercial (L-LC) zone, for the property located at 1988 Village Park Way.
2025-08-13 Item 10A 7-11 Appeal

2025-08-13 Item 10B Youth Commission Add Alternates
2025-08-13 Item 10B Youth Commission Add Alternates - Staff Presentation
2025-08-13 Item 10B Youth Commission Add Alternates - Public Comment
10C.
Consider local Municipal Code amendments which modify the 2025 California Building Standards Code related to building safety, fire prevention, energy efficiency and green building, in alignment with the City's Climate Action Plan goals and targets. Environmental Considerations: The amendments proposed will not have a significant effect on the environment because the strengthened requirements reduce hazards and accommodate features to reduce environmental effects. Adoption of the amendments is exempt from environmental review as per Section 15308 of the CEQA Guidelines, which allows a categorical exemption for "actions taken by regulatory. agencies, as authorized by state or local ordinance, to assure the maintenance, restoration, enhancement, or protection of the environment where the regulatory process involves procedures for protection of the environment." Furthermore, the amendments related to energy efficiency and green building were previously evaluated in the Final Negative Declaration (ND) for the Climate Action Plan (Case No. 17-224), dated December 5, 2017, and Addendum to the ND (Case No. ENV-004106-2020), dated Oct 20, 2020. The ND and the Addendum evaluated the potential environmental effects of the implementation of the Climate Action Plan, including the adoption and enforcement of energy efficiency and renewable energy ordinances. This project is within the scope of the Final Negative Declaration and the Addendum, and no further California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) compliance is required. Contact Persons: Principal Planner Maynard, Sustainability Manager Najera, and Interim Fire Marshall Villagomez
Direct staff to prepare ordinances for City Council consideration, to adopt local Municipal Code amendments which modify the 2025 California Building Standards Code, and continue the following existing local codes which require enhanced building safety, fire prevention, energy efficiency and green building regulation, with minor changes: 1) Building Code Amendments (EMC 23.12.030.B); 2) Fire Code Amendments (EMC 10.04.020); 3) Electric Readiness (EMC 23.12.080.J); 4) Existing Building Energy Efficiency (EMC 23.12.080.D and E); 5) Electric Vehicle Charging (EMC 23.12.110.E); and 6) Graywater Systems (EMC 23.12.110.D).

2025-08-13 Item 12A Council Initiated item O'Hara - Ordinance 9.01.010
2025-08-13 Items 12A 12B & 12C Public Comment

Council initiated item from Council Member Jim O’Hara regarding amending Encinitas Municipal Code 14.40.145 regarding the restricted hours for parking recreational vehicles on public streets and property.
Environmental Considerations: The action being considered by the City Council is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) because it is not a “project” under Section 15378(b)(5) of CEQA Guidelines. The action involves an organizational or administrative activity of government that will not result in the direct or indirect physical change in the environment.
Direct staff to draft the necessary revisions to Municipal Code 14.40.145, updating the restricted parking hours to reflect the new timeframe. The revised code should clarify that all recreational vehicles—including trailers, camper trailers, boats and trailers, cab-over campers, motorhomes, and vans or van conversions used for habitation or camping—are subject to these regulations unless they display a valid permit under section 14.40.150.
2025-08-13 Item 12B Council Initiated item O'Hara - Code 14.40.145

Notice to the Public:
To ensure that the City meets your needs when addressing the City Council, all presentation materials which require the use of visual equipment need to be submitted to the City's IT Division at least 24 hours in advance of the meeting (except for appeal hearings where materials must be submitted 7 days in advance). This includes photographs, Microsoft Office documents (PowerPoint, Word, Excel). No CD's, DVD's, or USB thumb/flash drives will be accepted at the meeting. All materials must be in PC format and digital presentation items must be emailed to it-service-desk@encinitasca.gov . Please label all materials with the corresponding agenda item number. Should technical assistance be necessary, it will be available to presenters from 5:30 p.m. to 5:50 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Presentation of video/digital/photographs are considered part of the maximum time limit provided to speakers.
